entradas.descripcion: What you do NOT want: artifacts, text, deformations, the wrong style. Only some models support it.
What you DO want to appear: subject, style, lighting, camera, atmosphere, quality.
The prompt is the text description you give the AI model so it generates an image, video or audio. The more specific, the better the result.
Tags = comma-separated keywords (Stable Diffusion style). Natural = descriptive sentences (Midjourney/GPT style).
Parameter that controls up to which neural-network layer is used. 1 = all, 2 = less detail (more artistic). For Anime: 2, Realism: 1.
Selective focus effect: sharp subject, blurred background. Tags: 'depth of field', 'bokeh', 'f/1.4', 'background blur'.
'Cyberpunk', 'Art Nouveau', 'Art Deco', 'Baroque', 'Impressionist', 'Photorealistic', 'Anime', 'Synthwave', 'Solarpunk'.
Similar to CFG but in FLUX models. Controls adherence to the prompt. Typical values: 1-3 (turbo), 3.5-7.5 (standard).
Type of light in the scene. 'Golden hour', 'blue hour', 'rim lighting', 'volumetric lighting', 'neon glow', 'soft diffused'.
Type of framing: 'wide shot', 'close-up', 'medium shot', 'extreme close-up', 'aerial view', 'dutch angle'.
Parameter (Midjourney) that controls how much the result deviates from the prompt. Low = faithful, high = unexpected. Ideal for exploring.
Additional model that controls the image composition via maps (poses, edges, depth). Lets you specify exactly where each element goes.
Technique that starts from an existing image (not AI-generated) and transforms it. In Stable Diffusion: load image → adjust prompt → generate. Produces more controllable results.
In FLUX you can use :: to separate weights: 'red::1.5 blue::0.5 green'. In SD: (tag:1.3)(tag:0.8). In Midjourney: ::0.5 after the word.
Output resolution. 512x512 = fast, 1024x1024 = standard, 2048+ = high quality. Later upscaling improves details without increasing generation time.
Style reference that tells the model what kind of art to imitate. In Midjourney: '--style', in DALL-E: 'style: photography/painting/3d'.
Extracts the 'genetic fingerprint' of an image as structured JSON: subject, scene, lighting, camera, style, composition, atmosphere, technical data. Used to replicate the style in other images.
Compares a loaded image with your current prompt. Shows: % match, matching elements, elements missing from your prompt, extra elements you didn't ask for. Ideal for improving prompts.
Reviews your last 10 prompts from history and for each suggests: what's good, what to improve, an improved version. Helps you spot improvement patterns.
Generates multiple prompts at once using a list or pattern. Ideal for creating series of variations or preparing catalog content.
The LLM analyzes your last 30 prompts and tells you: what kind of content you generate, which models/platforms you prefer, which styles you use most, what you could explore further.
Hides UI elements so you focus only on writing. Shows only: idea, output, generate button. Perfect for intense writing sessions.
Combinations of variables + predefined logic that generate structured prompts. E.g.: 'Portrait [adjective] + [subject] + [setting] + [style] + [lighting]'.
Shortcuts that insert predefined blocks of text. E.g.: insert a negative preset, a lighting formula, a camera structure. Used with quick buttons or keyboard shortcuts.
Save characters with a name, description and notes. They are inserted into prompts to keep consistency across image series. Includes an associated LoRA if it has one.
Predefined prompt structures with variables (subject, setting, style). Let you generate complete prompts by filling in only what changes. There are some per mode (image/video/audio) and per style.
Your best prompts, saved with a rating (1-10) and the model used. Mark them as favorites for quick access and to compare what makes a prompt excellent.
Ultra-fast generation using turbo models. Ideal for iterating ideas without waiting. Only works with models marked as 'Turbo' in the config.

Rates the quality of your prompt across 4 categories (25 pts each): Subject clarity, Style detail, Composition and camera, Quality and atmosphere. Green ≥80%, yellow 50-79%, red <50%. Suggests improvements automatically.
Save seeds you liked to reuse them. Applying a seed automatically loads: model, platform, sampler, steps, CFG, clip skip and resolution. Ideal for keeping visual coherence across a series.
Small reusable fragments: quality tags (8k, intricate), camera setups, lights, styles. Inserted with one click or a keyboard shortcut.
Generates 3 variants of the current prompt: one more concise, one more descriptive, one with a different focus. Useful for exploring creative directions.
Controls how faithfully the model follows your prompt. Low (1-3) = more creative, High (7-15) = stricter.
Models like Midjourney, GPT Image, FLUX understand full sentences. Do NOT use tags or numeric weights with these.
A small model that 'plugs into' the main model to add a specific style, character or concept.
'Magic' tags that improve quality in SD. Careful: overusing them degrades it. 1-2 at the end of the prompt is enough.
Models optimized for speed (Z Image Turbo, FLUX Schnell). They generate in seconds but with low CFG (~1) — they IGNORE weights and negative prompt.
Increase the importance of a tag. (tag:1.5) boosts, (tag:0.7) reduces. Only in Stable Diffusion models.
Image proportions. 1:1 = square, 16:9 = horizontal, 9:16 = vertical, 2:3 = portrait, 21:9 = cinema.
Algorithm that decides how the model builds the image. Euler = fast, DPM++ = balanced, Karras = high quality.
Random number that defines the variations. Same seed + same prompt = the exact same image. Useful for iterating and comparing.
How many iterations the model does. More steps = more detail but slower. Turbo: 4-8, Standard: 20-30, HQ: 50+.
Keywords that activate a LoRA. E.g.: 'sks dog' for a dog LoRA. They go at the start of the prompt.
Repeats generate→score→improve until it reaches the score you set (or N iterations), always keeping the best version. Different from one-off Scoring. Shortcut Ctrl+Shift+O.
Conversational assistant for your prompt: you ask for changes in natural language ('darker', 'add fog') and it rewrites it respecting the model's format.
Rewrites the current prompt to the exact format of the selected model (natural vs tags, weights, max_chars, negatives) without changing the idea. Available in 🛠 Tools and as a Macro step.
Generates N panels (3-12) with shot type and a description per panel, keeping visual coherence. Image mode only. Shortcut Ctrl+Shift+B.
Converts the current image prompt into a video one for Veo/Sora/Kling/Seedance, adding camera movement, duration and number of shots.
Turns a professional brief into 5 different prompt proposals. Designed for commissioned work.
Generates a dataset to train a character LoRA: up to 24 angles with the SAME identity + kohya captions. Starts from a text sheet, an automatic one or a reference photo.
Shows the session's spending per provider and per model, the total and the history. Shortcut Ctrl+Shift+M. Each model has its own price per million tokens.
Control panel: statistics, activity from recent days, most used mode/platform, achievements and the challenge of the day. Shortcut Ctrl+Shift+D.
Groups prompts and their setup by job, so you don't mix up different campaigns. Each project remembers its configuration.
With the 🖼 Ref switch on, Img→Prompt does not copy the literal image: it extracts only its visual GUIDANCE (palette, light, style) to create a NEW scene with that aesthetic.
Four narrative generators: Mood (tone/atmosphere), Story (sequence with beginning-middle-end), Board (board of scenes) and Walk (tour through an environment).
Each model supports a maximum number of characters in the prompt; going over makes it trim or ignore the end. G-Prompt knows it per model and warns or adapts the prompt to respect it.
